When the tank is nearly empty, we want to push on a little further; when a warning light comes on, we often tell ourselves it can wait until we are less busy.

It is more like a partner sharing the drive, with its own signals and its own rhythm. The soul knows where it wants to go; the body reminds us how much strength we have left right now, and whether we need to rest.
我們把這樣的關係稱為「共駕」：方向可以一起看，路可以一起走。當身體傳來訊號，我們: We call this relationship “co-driving”: we can look at the direction together, and travel the road together. When the body sends a signal, we are willing to stop and listen, and to let it take part in the decisions that come next.
這是我們理解自己的一種方式，不是已經被證實的定律。: This is one way we understand ourselves, not a law that has been proven.

02 身體是執行者，也是夥伴: 02　The body does the work, and is a partner too
好好照顧它，也是對自己負責。: Taking good care of it is taking responsibility for ourselves.
「要尊重地球的遊戲規則。我們就是肉做的。」: “Respect the rules of the game on Earth. We are made of flesh and blood.”
「肉身是很重要的執行者夥伴，我們就得好好照顧他。」: “The physical body is a very important partner that carries things out, so we have to take good care of it.”
想法可以走得很遠，但要真正走出去，還是需要這副身體陪我們一步一步完成。睡不好、吃: Ideas can travel far, but to really set out, we still need this body to go with us, step by step. When we sleep badly, eat badly, or never find time to rest, we may find the strength is not there, even when we know in our hearts what we want to do.
我們希望慢慢練習，把照顧身體放回生活裡。不必等到所有事情都忙完，才允許自己好好睡: We hope to practice, slowly, putting care for the body back into everyday life. There is no need to wait until everything is done before we allow ourselves to sleep well and eat well; and rest does not have to be a reward we only earn after working hard.
睡眠、飲食和休息，是每天生活的一部分，也是讓兩個駕駛都保持清醒的基本功。: Sleep, food and rest are part of everyday life, and they are the basics that keep both drivers alert.
身體不是障礙，是基礎。它一直都在陪我們走這段路，值得被好好對待。: The body is not an obstacle; it is the foundation. It has been with us on this road all along, and it deserves to be treated well.

03 可以檢查的這一段：累的時候，判斷也會跟著累: 03　The part we can check: when you are tired, your judgment gets tired too
不一定走得比較快。: does not always get you there faster.
有時候，我們會以為，只有撐過極限、經歷足夠的辛苦，才算真正努力過，也才會有所成長: Sometimes we think that only by pushing past our limits and going through enough hardship have we truly made an effort, and that only then will we grow.
但我們想試著提供另一種可能：成長，不必等到崩潰。也可以在還有餘裕的時候，慢慢學會: But we want to offer another possibility: growth does not have to wait until you break down. It can also happen while you still have something in reserve, as you slowly learn to rest, sort through your thoughts, and find a pace that suits you.
關於睡眠、壓力和休息，有幾項研究可以參考：: On sleep, stress and rest, there are a few studies we can look to:
睡不夠，判斷也可能受到影響: Too little sleep can affect judgment
：一篇回顧文章整理了睡眠不足對認知功能的影響。除了注意力和反應速度，較複雜的思考: : A review brought together research on how sleep deprivation affects cognitive function. Beyond attention and reaction speed, more complex thinking, judgment and decision-making may also be affected.
睡眠和情緒也有關係: Sleep and emotion are linked too
：一篇研究回顧指出，睡眠不足時，大腦對負面事件的情緒反應可能更強烈，調節情緒也可: : A research review points out that when we are short of sleep, the brain's emotional reactions to negative events may be stronger, and regulating emotions may become harder.
壓力大的時候，可能更容易依照習慣反應: Under heavy stress, we may fall back on habit more easily
：一篇回顧文章整理了動物與人的研究，指出壓力可能暫時影響前額葉參與思考與規劃的功: : A review of animal and human research points out that stress may temporarily affect the part the prefrontal cortex plays in thinking and planning, making us more likely to follow the reactions we already know.
短暫休息，也有它的價值: Short breaks have their value too
：一篇統合分析整理了多項研究，發現工作中 10 分鐘以內的短暫休息，有助於提升活: : A meta-analysis pooling a number of studies found that short breaks of 10 minutes or less during work help raise vigor and reduce fatigue. Whether they also improve work performance depends on the type of work and the length of the break.
「共駕」是我們理解自己的說法與信念；研究提供的，是關於睡眠、壓力和休息的參考。研: “Co-driving” is our way of understanding ourselves, and a belief; what research offers is a reference on sleep, stress and rest. Research supports the part that can be observed, and is not used to prove our belief.

04 累了還硬撐，是哪一種力量在開車: 04　Tired but still pushing on: which power is driving?
有些力量，讓我們很能撐。: Some powers make us very good at holding on.
但也可能讓身體的聲音，慢慢被忽略。: But they can also let the body's voice slowly go unheard.
12 語根，是每個人身上都有的 12 種力量。這些力量在適當的時候，可以成為我們: The 12 Root Codes are 12 powers that everyone carries. At the right moments, these powers can be our strengths; but when one of them is used too much, it can also lead us to overlook the body's needs without realizing it.
節奏帶動的力量（Ori'shan）: The power of setting the rhythm (Ori'shan)
用過頭時：身體僵硬、表達受限，情緒卡在身體裡，容易焦慮、倦怠。: when overused: your body stiffens, expression gets blocked and emotions get stuck in your body, and you easily become anxious and worn out.
領航創造的力量（Nael'tu）: The power of navigating and creating (Nael'tu)
用過頭時：控制慾變強、過度承擔，壓力都堆在自己身上，越領導越孤單。: when overused: the urge to control grows and you take on too much; the pressure all piles up on you, and the more you lead, the lonelier it gets.
用過頭時：壓抑感覺、迴避衝突，表面平靜，其實把自己關了起來，身體僵硬、關係疏離。: when overused: you suppress your feelings and avoid conflict; you look calm on the surface, but you have actually shut yourself in, your body stiffens, and relationships drift.
每一種力量都有它珍貴的地方。我們不需要否定它，也不必急著改變自己。: Every power has something precious in it. We do not need to deny it, nor rush to change ourselves.
只是當我們發現，自己又開始習慣性地硬撐，也許可以先問問：現在的身體，還跟得上嗎？: It is only that when we notice ourselves pushing on out of habit again, we might first ask: can my body keep up right now?

05 一個小練習：問一下車況: 05　A small practice: check on the car
開車前會看看油錶，: Before a drive, we glance at the fuel gauge;
生活裡，也可以問問自己的狀態。: in daily life, we can check on how we are doing, too.
我們每天都會安排很多事情，卻不一定記得問問自己，今天還有多少力氣。: Every day we plan a lot of things, but we do not always remember to ask ourselves how much strength we have today.
可以試著找一個固定的時間，例如早上起床、午餐後，或是睡前，花 30 秒問自己三個: Try picking a set time, such as when you wake up, after lunch, or before bed, and spend 30 seconds asking yourself three questions:
身體現在的電量，大概還有幾成？: Roughly how much battery does my body have left right now?
今天有沒有好好吃飯、喝水？昨晚睡得夠嗎？: Have I eaten properly and drunk enough water today? Did I sleep enough last night?
如果電量不到一半，今天可以少做哪一件事？: If the battery is below half, what is one thing I can do less of today?
問完，不需要急著改變什麼，也不用立刻找到答案。只是慢慢練習，把注意力放回自己身上: Once you have asked, there is no need to rush to change anything, or to find an answer right away. Just keep practicing, slowly, bringing your attention back to yourself and listening to what your body is telling you.
如果願意，也可以先跟自己約好一句：「電量低於三成，我就先休息十分鐘。」: If you like, you can also make a promise to yourself in advance: “When my battery drops below 30%, I will rest for ten minutes first.”
不一定每次都記得，也不用每次都做到。想起來的時候，再問一次就好。: You will not remember every time, and you do not have to manage it every time. Whenever you remember, just ask once more.
「我看到好多人活得很耗損 我想建立一個不耗損的場域」: “I see so many people living in a way that wears them down. I want to build a space that doesn't wear people down.”
我們希望，有更多人能在生活裡，慢慢找到不必一直硬撐的方式。: We hope more people can slowly find ways of living that do not mean always pushing through.
好好睡覺、好好吃飯，累了就允許自己休息一下。有時候，只是比昨天早一點聽見身體的聲: Sleep well, eat well, and when you are tired, allow yourself a little rest. Sometimes simply hearing your body a little earlier than you did yesterday is already a very good start.
活得不耗損，也是一種前進。: Living without wearing yourself down is a way forward too.

我們相信，靈魂和身體是一起開車的夥伴。彼此陪伴，也彼此尊重，誰都不是誰的工具。: We believe the soul and the body are partners driving together. They keep each other company and respect each other; neither is the other's tool.
我們相信，成長不一定需要經歷痛苦，也不必等到崩潰才開始。這是我們理解自己的方式，: We believe growth does not necessarily require going through pain, and does not have to wait until we break down to begin. This is how we understand ourselves; it is not a scientific conclusion, and it does not need everyone to agree.
睡得比較充足的那幾天，自己的判斷和情緒是否比較穩定？可以簡單記錄，過一段時間再回: On the days you sleep enough, are your judgment and emotions steadier? You can keep a simple record and look back after a while.
覺得累的時候，先休息十分鐘。回來之後，做事的感覺有沒有不同？可以從自己的生活裡試: When you feel tired, rest for ten minutes first. When you come back, does your work feel any different? You can try it in your own life.
持續練習「問車況」一段時間後，有沒有比較早察覺自己正在疲累、需要休息？不必急著得: After practicing “checking on the car” for a while, do you notice sooner that you are getting tired and need rest? No need to hurry to an answer; just observe slowly.
